Routing evidence:
- Option C was rejected for all observed claims, refunds, and east-region shipments, regardless of size or urgency.
- Option C was accepted once for a small shipment from the north region (REQ-2408), where the displayed label began “regional…”.
- Treat C as a narrow regional-office route, apparently valid for north-region shipments only; do not select it by default.
- No successful evidence yet distinguishes A (standard queue) from B (priority desk). “Large,” repeated requests, or “second attempt” may indicate priority, but this is unconfirmed.
- When options/labels are truncated or malformed, rely on the explicit valid choices and avoid inferring that C is valid merely because “regional office” appears in the message.

Routing evidence:
- Option C was previously rejected for observed claims, refunds, and east-region shipments, but was accepted once for a small north-region shipment (REQ-2408) with a “regional…” label. Treat C as a possible regional-office route, not a default; its region and eligibility remain uncertain.
- New evidence: A was accepted for a small east claim (REQ-2410), a large south shipment (REQ-2416), and a small south claim (REQ-2418).
- A was rejected for a large north invoice (REQ-2411) and a small east shipment (REQ-2417). Thus size, region, and request type matter; “no rush” does not reliably imply A.
- B was rejected for every new trial (REQ-2412–2415 and REQ-2419), including large/second-attempt requests and repeated or regional-office wording. Do not select B based only on urgency, size, repetition, or “second attempt.”
- The rejected B cases suggest C may be the likely alternative, but there is no confirmed successful C evidence for these patterns. Do not treat “regional office” wording alone as proof.
- When labels/options are truncated or malformed, rely only on explicit valid choices and avoid inferring C from partial text.

Routing evidence:
- A is supported for: small east claim (REQ-2410), large south shipment (REQ-2416), small south claim (REQ-2418), large south claims (REQ-2422, REQ-2426), and small east invoice (REQ-2423).
- A is rejected for north requests tested: large north invoice (REQ-2411) and small north claim (REQ-2420). It was also rejected for a small east shipment (REQ-2417). Region, request type, and size matter; “no rush,” repetition, or routine wording are not reliable A signals.
- C was accepted only once: small north shipment REQ-2408 with “regional…” wording. C was rejected for a large north shipment (REQ-2425) and large north claim (REQ-2429). Treat C as uncertain and do not infer it from “regional office” wording alone.
- B was rejected in every recorded trial (REQ-2412–2415, REQ-2419), including urgent, large, repeated, second-attempt, and regional-office cases. Do not select B based on those cues.
- Recent malformed/truncated cases reinforce that D is not a valid option (REQ-2421, REQ-2424, REQ-2427, REQ-2428). Never invent D; use only explicitly listed valid choices.
- For partially truncated option lists, rely strictly on visible valid options. Do not infer the intended route from wording, sender department, urgency, paperwork format, or prior similarity.

Routing evidence:
- A accepted for south requests tested: large shipment (REQ-2416), small claim (REQ-2418, REQ-2433, REQ-2439), large claims (REQ-2422, REQ-2426), large invoice (REQ-2435), and small invoice (REQ-2438); also small east claim (REQ-2410) and small east invoice (REQ-2423).
- A rejected for north requests tested: large invoice (REQ-2411, REQ-2430) and small claim (REQ-2420). It was also rejected for small east shipment (REQ-2417) and large east invoice (REQ-2437). Region, request type, and size matter; urgency, repetition, routine wording, sender department, and paperwork format are not reliable A signals.
- C accepted only once: small north shipment REQ-2408 with “regional…” wording. C was rejected for large north shipment (REQ-2425), large north claim (REQ-2429, REQ-2432), north large invoice (REQ-2430), north small invoice (REQ-2434), north small refund (REQ-2436), and small east shipment (REQ-2431). It was also rejected when the visible label was truncated. Treat C as uncertain; never infer it from “regional office” wording.
- B was rejected in every recorded trial (REQ-2412–2415, REQ-2419). Do not select B based on urgency, repetition, size, or regional wording.
- Malformed/truncated cases reinforce that D is not valid (REQ-2421, REQ-2424, REQ-2427, REQ-2428). Never invent D; use only explicitly listed valid choices.
- For partially truncated option lists, rely strictly on visible valid options. Do not infer the route from wording, sender department, urgency, paperwork format, or prior similarity.

Routing evidence:
- A accepted for south requests: large/small shipments, claims, and invoices (REQ-2416, REQ-2418, REQ-2433, REQ-2439, REQ-2422, REQ-2426, REQ-2435, REQ-2438, REQ-2443, REQ-2445, REQ-2448, REQ-2449). Also accepted for small east claim/invoice (REQ-2410, REQ-2423) and large north shipment (REQ-2444).
- A rejected for east shipments (small: REQ-2417, REQ-2440, REQ-2446) and large east invoices (REQ-2437, REQ-2442); rejected for north large invoices (REQ-2411, REQ-2430) and small claim (REQ-2420). Thus region, request type, and size matter; do not generalize from wording or superficial similarity.
- C accepted only for small north shipment REQ-2408. C rejected for large north shipment/claims, north invoices/refund, and east shipments/invoices (including REQ-2447); truncated labels also provide no support. Treat C as uncertain and never infer it from “regional office” wording.
- B was rejected in every recorded trial (REQ-2412–2415, REQ-2419). Never select B based on urgency, repetition, size, or regional wording.
- Malformed/truncated cases reinforce that D is invalid (REQ-2421, REQ-2424, REQ-2427, REQ-2428). Never invent D; use only explicitly visible valid choices.
- For partially truncated option lists, rely strictly on visible valid options. Sender department, urgency, repetition, routine wording, and paperwork format are not reliable routing signals.

Routing evidence:
- A is accepted for all tested south requests: large/small shipments, claims, and invoices; also east small claim/invoice and large claim, and north large shipment (REQ-2408, REQ-2410, REQ-2422, REQ-2423, REQ-2416, REQ-2418, REQ-2433, REQ-2435, REQ-2438, REQ-2439, REQ-2443, REQ-2444, REQ-2445, REQ-2448, REQ-2449, REQ-2450, REQ-2452, REQ-2455, REQ-2458, REQ-2459).
- A is rejected for east shipments (small), large east invoices, east refunds (small and large), north large invoices, north large claims, and north small claims/refunds. Region, request type, and size matter; do not generalize from wording or superficial similarity.
- Recent confirmations: east large claims and north large shipments accept A; east small/large refunds, east large invoice, north large claim, and north small refund reject A.
- B was rejected in every recorded trial. Never choose B based on urgency, repetition, size, region, or wording.
- C has no reliable positive evidence; earlier apparent “C accepted” records were actually A selections. Treat C as uncertain and never infer it from “regional office” wording. Truncated labels provide no support.
- Malformed/truncated cases reinforce that D is invalid. Never invent D; use only explicitly visible valid choices.
- Sender department, urgency, repetition, routine wording, scanned/typed paperwork, and format are not reliable routing signals.

Routing evidence:
- A is accepted for south large/small shipments, claims, and invoices; south large claim and invoice reconfirmed (REQ-2467, REQ-2469).
- A is rejected for south large refunds (REQ-2461, REQ-2462, REQ-2463, REQ-2468). Do not generalize A across request types.
- A is accepted for east small claims (REQ-2466) and previously for east small claims/invoices and large claims. A is rejected for east shipments (including large, REQ-2464), east refunds (small/large), and large east invoices.
- A is rejected for north small invoices (REQ-2460), north large invoices, north large claims, and north small claims/refunds. A is accepted for north large shipments.
- Region, request type, and size matter; wording and superficial similarity are unreliable.
- B was rejected in every recorded trial. Never choose B based on urgency, repetition, size, region, or wording.
- C has no reliable positive evidence; the sole recent C trial (north large invoice, REQ-2465) was rejected. Earlier apparent C successes were actually A selections. Never infer C from “regional office” wording or truncated labels.
- Malformed/truncated options provide no support for any label and reinforce that D is invalid. Use only explicitly visible valid choices; do not invent missing options.
- Sender department, urgency, repetition, routine wording, scanned/typed paperwork, and format are not reliable routing signals.
